trust_decision.summary: applyRateLimit decides which quota bucket an anonymous HTTP caller consumes; with no trusted client IP every anonymous caller shares one ip:unknown:<kind> bucket, so any direct caller of *.convex.site can drain the quota for all visitors (and with the opt-in flag, caller-chosen forwarded headers pick the bucket and the download-metric identity).

landing_point.why: The summary says 'quota exhaustion via anonymous API'. The anonymous bucket key and the getClientIp fallback to 'unknown' are in applyRateLimit, the single primitive every route calls.

fix_sites.entry_point: every anonymous public HTTP route via installRateLimitedRoutes wrapper (convex/lib/httpRouteRateLimit.ts:100) and direct handler calls (e.g. convex/downloads.ts:113)
same: the anonymous branch of applyRateLimit now returns a 307 redirect or 401 instead of consuming the shared bucket (fix.diff:766-767, 808-866)
same; the ip:unknown key is removed (fix.diff:776-780)

getClientIp, also read by download-metric identity mappers: GET /api/v1/download (convex/downloads.ts:379,406), package download/artifact routes (convex/httpApiV1/packagesV1.ts:807,4763); now reads only a WeakMap filled by applyRateLimit (fix.diff:786-799)

router-level default limit: package-inspector worker routes, /api/internal/archive-download-metric, /api/auth/signin|callback are exempted so they are not redirected away from the Convex origin (fix.diff:916-944)
new convex/lib/verifiedClientIp.ts: verifies Vercel OIDC token + x-clawhub-client-ip, canonicalises IPv4/IPv6, has a loopback dev exception

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The proxy is in a separate front-end server package, and it already sends an OIDC identity for archive requests only (server/convexProxy.ts:144). A solver can argue that edge header hygiene is a deployment concern, especially since the specs present the shared fallback bucket as the intended design (specs/rate-limiting.md:14-17, docs/http-api.md:82-85).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Credentialed handlers at the Convex origin must keep working: package-inspector worker bearer routes, signed archive-metric receipts, and OAuth sign-in/callback. API-token users keep per-user quotas, and the local loopback dev deployment still works. An over-broad 'reject unverified anonymous' breaks them or creates a redirect loop.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Scope the ip:unknown bucket per route or raise its limit, or reject anonymous callers outright, without designing a verified edge identity, fixing the proxy or exempting the credentialed worker/OAuth routes.

out_of_scope_notes: Non-HTTP Convex queries/mutations reached via the Convex client websocket are not covered by applyRateLimit; not examined.
src/lib/packageApi.ts:255-280 SSR fetches forward raw client IP headers; after the fix these are ignored, so SSR anonymous reads may be redirected. This was not addressed in the fix diff.

Main concern for fairness: the published fix is a new trust design (Vercel OIDC assertion plus x-clawhub-client-ip header, 307 redirect to SITE_URL, a 401 for invalid assertions to avoid loops). Hidden tests coupled to these header names and status codes cannot be derived from a short report, and the in-repo specs (specs/rate-limiting.md:14-17) present the shared fallback bucket as intended. None of the defined O12 flags captures this, so it is listed here.
Lessons-v2 records resource-exhaustion tasks as 0 of 7 hard; this advisory is CWE-770 although its mechanism is identity trust rather than an algorithmic loop.
